1.s: Which of the following correctly describes food irradiation?
o: It is identical to food adulteration.
It uses only magnetic fields to reconstruct food images.
It always increases the need for chemical preservatives and refrigeration.
It uses ionising radiation to destroy harmful organisms without altering nutrition substantially.

1.sec: Food technology - additives, adulterants, preservation, fortification, cold chain, packaging

1.s: The chemical change caused by radiolytic products during food irradiation is described as:

1.sec: Food technology - additives, adulterants, preservation, fortification, irradiation, cold chain, packaging

1.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Department of Atomic Energy has installed 25 food irradiators in PPP mode.
2. Gamma rays can extend the shelf life of potatoes and onions to eight months without cold storage.
3. Irradiation necessarily requires refrigeration after treatment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
1.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Irradiation can extend shelf life without cold storage, so statement 3 is false.
1.tq: Check the numerical facts and reject the reversed preservation claim.
1.sec: Food technology - additives, adulterants, preservation, fortification, irradiation, cold chain, packaging

1.s: With reference to the Cold Chain scheme of PM Kisan Sampada Yojana, which one of the following is correct?
o: MoFPI funds multi-product irradiation units; 16 were approved and 9 were operational in August 2025.
MoFPI funds thermal-receipt units; 25 were approved and all were operational in August 2025.
DAE funds fair price shops; 9 were approved and 16 were operational in August 2025.
FSSAI funds 25 MRI units; 16 were approved and 9 were operational in August 2025.

Milk with brick powder; rice with Sudan dyes; salt with argemone oil
Oil with lead chromate; turmeric with vitamin D; milk with metanil yellow
Rice with only preservatives; salt with only emulsifiers; milk with only MSG

1.s:
Consider the following pairs:

2. Digital payments — e-governance
3. Screen time — sedentary life and eye strain
4. Digital technology — cyber fraud

Biometric surveillance and risk-scoring used in food, health, pension and scholarship delivery
Gamma irradiation used only for potatoes and onions
Blockchain used exclusively for PDS route optimisation

1.x: Disease mapping uses geospatial technology to identify and visualise disease hotspots.

1. Aarogya Setu used Bluetooth and GPS for COVID-19 contact tracing.
2. Facility location may consider population distribution and travel time.

1.s: Microwave ovens heat food primarily because microwaves of approximately which frequency cause water molecules to rotate?

1.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the vapour-compression cycle in a refrigerator?
o: The refrigerant releases heat while evaporating inside the refrigerator and absorbs it at the condenser.
Water absorbs heat at the condenser and releases it in the freezer.
The refrigerant absorbs heat while evaporating inside the refrigerator and releases it at the condenser.
The refrigerant produces cold by electromagnetic induction in the storage chamber.
1.x: In a vapour-compression refrigerator, the refrigerant absorbs heat while evaporating inside and releases heat at the condenser.
1.tq: Follow the direction of heat transfer rather than relying on the familiar but imprecise idea that the refrigerator creates cold.
1.sec: Household appliances → working principle  [other exams]

1.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. An induction cooktop works through electromagnetic induction.
2. Eddy currents are produced in a ferromagnetic vessel such as an iron or steel vessel.
3. The cooking vessel is heated mainly by combustion of LPG.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
1.x: Induction cooking uses electromagnetic induction and eddy currents in a ferromagnetic vessel. It does not heat the vessel by LPG combustion.
1.tq: Reject the statement that substitutes a nearby household technology for the actual working principle.

o: using electromagnetic induction in a steel container
applying pressure against osmosis to push water through a semi-permeable membrane
boiling water at a pressure of about 120°C

The cooker converts water directly into ice vapour.

It introduced innovation as the central theme for the first time

2.s: Which of the following measures reflects the equity dimension of the Draft STIP 2020?
o: Inclusion of women, marginalised groups and LGBTQ+ persons, along with day-care facilities at funded laboratories
Exclusion of marginalised communities from research governance
Restriction of funded laboratories to male researchers
Removal of social support from scientific institutions
2.x: The Draft STIP 2020 proposed inclusion of women, marginalised groups and LGBTQ+ persons and also envisaged day-care facilities at funded laboratories.
2.tq: Recognise the option that combines the policy’s stated inclusion and support measures.
2.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

2.s:
Which of the following was associated with the Draft STIP 2020’s proposed international and knowledge-engagement measures?
1. Diaspora portal
2. Diplomacy for S&T
3. Traditional Knowledge Systems and grassroots innovators
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
2.x: The Draft STIP 2020 included a diaspora portal, Diplomacy for S&T, and support for Traditional Knowledge Systems and grassroots innovators.
2.tq: Check all listed institutional and outreach measures before selecting the complete code.
2.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

2.s:
The Draft STIP 2020 proposed doubling which of the following every five years?
1. Full-time equivalent researchers
2. Gross expenditure on research and development
3. Private share of gross expenditure on research and development
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: The draft policy proposed doubling FTE researchers, GERD and the private share of GERD every five years.
2.tq: Track the repeated quantitative target and avoid omitting the private-sector component.
2.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

2.s: Which one of the following was NOT an outcome of the Draft STIP 2020?
2.x: Atal Innovation Mission was not an outcome of STIP 2020; it was set up by NITI Aayog in 2016 as a separate initiative promoting innovation among students. ONOS and RIEF were associated with the draft policy proposals.
2.tq: Use the separate-initiative trap: identify the programme established outside the policy.
2.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

2.s: Atal Innovation Mission was set up by NITI Aayog in:
2.x: Atal Innovation Mission was set up by NITI Aayog in 2016 and was a separate initiative from the Draft STIP 2020.
2.tq: Separate the establishment year of a related initiative from the year of the policy under examination.
2.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

2.s: One Nation, One Subscription was approved by the Union Cabinet in November 2024 with an approximate allocation of:
2.x: One Nation, One Subscription was approved in November 2024 with an allocation of about ₹6,000 crore for the period 2025–27.
2.tq: Check the figure, time period and approval year together; distractors alter one of these details.
2.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

2.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the STI Policy, 2013?
o: Risky Idea Fund — support for high-risk innovation
Fund for Innovations for Social Inclusion — socially inclusive innovation
One Nation, One Subscription — STI Policy, 2013
Small idea–small money — support for small innovative ideas
2.x: One Nation, One Subscription is associated with the Draft STIP 2020 and was approved in 2024, not with the STI Policy, 2013. The other three were associated with the 2013 policy.
2.tq: Catch the cross-policy substitution by matching each instrument to its correct policy period.
2.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

2.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the STI Policy, 2013:
1. It proposed intervention in about ten high-impact sectors.
2. It sought to use modern science to advance traditional knowledge.
3. It assigned agricultural research and development policy to the STI Policy rather than ICAR.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: The 2013 policy envisaged direct STI intervention in about ten high-impact sectors and the use of modern science for traditional knowledge. Agricultural R&D policy was left to ICAR, making statement 3 incorrect.
2.tq: Identify the reversed institutional responsibility in the third statement.
2.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

2.s: Which of the following proposed measures of the Draft STIP 2020 would most directly support accountability in science and technology governance?
o: Permanent continuation of every funded programme
2.x: Periodic review and exit strategies were proposed to improve accountability and enable the discontinuation or restructuring of programmes when necessary.
2.tq: Apply the governance principle to select the measure that creates review and corrective mechanisms.
2.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

2.s: The proposed Open Science Framework under the Draft STIP 2020 aimed at making publicly funded data available under which terms?
2.x: The Draft STIP 2020 proposed that publicly funded data should be made available under FAIR terms.
2.tq: Test the exact technical acronym instead of a similar-looking expansion.
2.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

2.s: Which one of the following policies specified a target of raising Gross Expenditure on Research and Development (GERD) to 2% of GDP by the end of the Tenth Five Year Plan?
2.x: The Science and Technology Policy, 2003 targeted an increase in GERD to 2% of GDP by the end of the Tenth Plan. The 1958 and 1983 policies did not state a numerical GERD target.
2.tq: Identify the policy linked to the specific numerical target.
2.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

2.s:
With reference to the GERD targets in India’s science and technology policies, consider the following statements:
1. The Scientific Policy Resolution, 1958 stated no numerical GERD target.
2. The Technology Policy Statement, 1983 stated no numerical GERD target.
3. The Science and Technology Policy, 2003 targeted GERD of 2% of GDP by the end of the Tenth Plan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: All three statements are correct. The 1958 and 1983 policies had no numerical GERD target, while the 2003 policy set a 2% of GDP target by the end of the Tenth Plan.
2.tq: Check each policy separately before selecting the coded combination.
2.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

2.s: The Science, Technology and Innovation Policy, 2013 envisaged GERD at 2% of GDP with which of the following additional features?
o: Private-sector spending being limited to one-fourth of public spending
GERD being financed exclusively by the Union Government
Abolition of public expenditure on research
2.x: The 2013 policy envisaged GERD at 2% of GDP, with private-sector spending matching public spending.
2.tq: Distinguish the matching private-sector contribution from exclusive public financing.
2.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

2.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal GERD-related target associated with the draft Science, Technology and Innovation Policy, 2020?
o: To raise GERD to 2% of GDP only once by the end of the Tenth Plan
To double the number of FTE researchers, GERD and the private share of GERD every five years
To maintain the existing level of GERD for five years
To eliminate private-sector participation in research funding
2.x: The draft STIP 2020 proposed doubling full-time-equivalent researchers, GERD and the private share of GERD every five years.
2.tq: Use the distinctive repeated-doubling target to identify the policy.
2.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

2.s: India’s GERD reached approximately what share of GDP in FY 2023–24, described as a 15-year high?
2.x: GERD reached about 0.84% of GDP in FY 2023–24, a 15-year high. The national aim nevertheless remains 2% of GDP.
2.tq: Separate the latest achieved value from the long-term national target.
2.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

2.s: Which of the following correctly states the 2026 recommendations concerning research and innovation funding?
o: GERD should reach 2% of GDP within four to five years through greater private-sector participation, along with creation of NISPG and Vigyan Nidhi
A National Institute for Science Policy and Governance should be abolished and fellowships decentralised
GERD should remain below 1% of GDP and public funding should replace private funding
The target is to double GERD within one year through the existing fellowship system only
2.x: The recommendations called for GERD to reach 2% of GDP within four to five years through the private sector, proposed NISPG, and suggested a unified fellowship called Vigyan Nidhi.
2.tq: Match the recommendation package rather than isolating one proposal.
2.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

2.s:
Consider the following statements about the Research, Development and Innovation Fund:
1. It has an approved size of ₹1 lakh crore.
2. ₹20,000 crore was provided for FY 2025–26.
3. It is intended to boost private research and development.
4. It is operated through a Special Purpose Fund in the ANRF.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: All four statements are correct. The RDI Fund has a ₹1 lakh crore size, includes ₹20,000 crore for FY 2025–26, promotes private R&D and operates through a Special Purpose Fund in ANRF.
2.tq: Test the fund’s size, annual allocation, purpose and institutional channel together.
2.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

2.s: The Research, Development and Innovation Fund is intended to be implemented over which period according to the stated estimates?
o: Six years, with another estimate referring to seven years
2.x: One estimate describes implementation over six years, while another source refers to seven years. The stated material therefore records both estimates.
2.tq: Watch for closely related duration figures rather than assuming a single period.
2.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

2.s: The Prime Minister’s Science, Technology and Innovation Advisory Council (PM-STIAC) was set up in:
2.x: PM-STIAC was set up in 2018.
2.tq: Directly associate the advisory council with its establishment year.
2.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

2.s: Who chairs the Prime Minister’s Science, Technology and Innovation Advisory Council?
2.x: PM-STIAC is chaired by the Principal Scientific Adviser.
2.tq: Apply the ‘who chairs this body?’ institutional-role test.
2.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

2.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser:
1. It was created in 1999.
2. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was the first Principal Scientific Adviser.
3. The Principal Scientific Adviser is the chief science and technology adviser to the Prime Minister and the Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: All three statements are correct. The office was created in 1999, A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was its first holder, and the PSA advises the Prime Minister and Cabinet on science and technology.
2.tq: Combine establishment, first office-holder and functional role in one institutional question.
2.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

2.s: Which one of the following is a statutory body established under the ANRF Act, 2023?
2.x: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) is a statutory body established under the ANRF Act, 2023.
2.tq: Distinguish a statutory body created by legislation from advisory offices and missions.
2.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

2.s: Which of the following correctly describes the leadership structure of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation?
o: The Minister of Finance is its President and the Minister of Education is its sole Vice-President
The Prime Minister is its President and the Ministers of Science and Technology and Education are Vice-Presidents
The Principal Scientific Adviser is its President and the Cabinet Secretary is its Vice-President
The President of India is its President and the Prime Minister is its Vice-President
2.x: The Prime Minister is the President of ANRF, while the Ministers of Science and Technology and Education are its Vice-Presidents.
2.tq: Use the constitutional-style office hierarchy to discriminate between authorities.
2.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

2.s: Which of the following statements about ANRF is NOT correct?
o: It provides strategic direction for research and innovation.
It pools public and private research and development resources.
Its entire proposed ₹50,000 crore funding for 2023–28 is to come from non-government sources.
It subsumed the Science and Engineering Research Board.
2.x: The proposed funding is ₹50,000 crore for 2023–28, of which about ₹36,000 crore is expected from non-government sources; therefore, the entire amount is not expected from non-government sources.
2.tq: Find the incorrect funding-composition statement rather than the incorrect institutional function.
2.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

2.s: The ANRF is associated with which of the following financial and institutional roles?
o: Replacement for the Department of Biotechnology
Custodian of the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund
Authority for fixing the national GERD percentage by constitutional amendment
Exclusive custodian of the Atal Innovation Mission budget
2.x: ANRF is the custodian of the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund. It is not a replacement for DST or DBT and does not fix GERD through constitutional amendment.
2.tq: Link the fund with its designated institutional custodian.
2.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

2.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the institution with its role or establishment detail?
o: DST — established in 1986 as the parent department of CSIR
DBT — established in 1971 as the nodal department for science policy
DSIR — established in 1985 and functioning as the parent department of CSIR
CSIR — established in 1971 as the Department of Biotechnology
2.x: The Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) was established in 1985 and is the parent department of CSIR. DST was established in 1971, DBT in 1986 and CSIR in 1942.
2.tq: Start with the sure institutional-year pair and reject swapped departments.
2.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

2.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Department of Science and Technology was established in 1971.
2. The Department of Biotechnology was established in 1986.
3. CSIR was established in 1942.
4. The Secretary of DSIR is the Director-General of CSIR.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: All four statements are correct. DST dates from 1971, DBT from 1986, CSIR from 1942, and the Secretary of DSIR serves as the Director-General of CSIR.
2.tq: Verify dates and the parent-department relationship independently.
2.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

2.s: PM-STIAC framed nine technology missions during which period?
2.x: PM-STIAC framed nine technology missions between October 2018 and January 2019.
2.tq: Use the narrow date range to distinguish the council’s mission-framing phase.
2.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

2.s: During India’s chairship of BRICS science and technology cooperation, which two organisations act as India’s lead agencies?
2.x: CSIR and the Department of Biotechnology act as India’s lead agencies for BRICS science and technology cooperation during India’s chairship.
2.tq: Identify the correct pair of lead agencies rather than a general policy body.
2.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

2.s: The National Innovation Council, established in 2010, was associated with which of the following?
o: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and the management of defence production
Sam Pitroda and the promotion of inclusive innovation
The Principal Scientific Adviser and the regulation of higher education
NITI Aayog and the preparation of the Five Year Plans
2.x: The National Innovation Council was established in 2010 under Sam Pitroda, with inclusive innovation as its goal.
2.tq: Pair the body with its chairperson and distinctive objective.
2.sec: Decade of Innovation (2010-2020)

2.s: Which of the following was a feature of the National Innovation Council’s approach?
o: Replacement of all state science councils by one central council
Withdrawal of innovation initiatives from the private sector
Restriction of innovation activities to defence laboratories
Creation of state and sectoral innovation councils
2.x: The National Innovation Council promoted inclusive innovation through state and sectoral innovation councils.
2.tq: Select the institutional mechanism that follows the stated inclusive-innovation objective.
2.sec: Decade of Innovation (2010-2020)

2.s: The Decade of Innovation led into which major policy, in which innovation was made central?
2.x: The Decade of Innovation led into the Science, Technology and Innovation Policy, 2013, which placed innovation at the centre of policy.
2.tq: Follow the policy sequence from the innovation decade to the later policy.
2.sec: Decade of Innovation (2010-2020)

2.s: The Scientific Policy Resolution, 1958 was introduced during which Five Year Plan?
2.x: The Scientific Policy Resolution, 1958 came during the Second Five Year Plan, which covered 1956–61.
2.tq: Place the policy within the correct Five Year Plan period.
2.sec: S&T in Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog documents

2.s: The Defence Research and Development Organisation was formed by merging which of the following?
o: TDE, DTDP and the Defence Science Organisation
2.x: DRDO was formed by merging the Technical Development Establishment, the Directorate of Technical Development and Production, and the Defence Science Organisation.
2.tq: Test the formation history through the exact component organisations.
2.sec: S&T in Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog documents

2.s: Which organisation is the nodal agency for improving India’s Global Innovation Index rank and also publishes the India Innovation Index?
2.x: NITI Aayog is the nodal agency for improving India’s GII rank and publishes the India Innovation Index.
2.tq: Identify the agency from its paired ranking and index functions.
2.sec: S&T in Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog documents

2.s: The third edition of the India Innovation Index, published by NITI Aayog, was released on:
2.x: The third edition of the India Innovation Index, dated 2021, was released on 21 July 2022.
2.tq: Distinguish the edition year from the actual release date.
2.sec: S&T in Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog documents

2.s: Which of the following is hosted by NITI Aayog?
2.x: NITI Aayog hosts the Atal Innovation Mission.
2.tq: Match the mission with its host institution.
2.sec: S&T in Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog documents

2.s: According to the Ease of Doing R&D in India report, approximately what share of ANRF funds goes to IITs?
2.x: The report states that approximately 80% of ANRF funds go to IITs and also points to slow approvals.
2.tq: Identify the magnitude of the institutional funding concentration.
2.sec: S&T in Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog documents

2.s: Which of the following is a role of State Councils of Science and Technology such as APCOST?
o: Issuing national patents and regulating all Union laboratories
Framing state science and technology policy, providing research grants and popularising science
Serving as the statutory governing council of ANRF
Determining India’s Global Innovation Index methodology
2.x: State S&T councils frame state S&T policy, provide research grants and popularise science. They do not perform the national statutory functions of ANRF or NITI Aayog.
2.tq: Apply the state-level institutional role to the functions listed.
2.sec: AP State Council of Science and Technology (APCOST) - state-level role

2.s: APCOST functions under which department of the Government of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Industries, Commerce and Information Technology Department
Higher Education and Skill Development Department
Environment, Forests, Science and Technology Department
2.x: APCOST works under the Andhra Pradesh Environment, Forests, Science and Technology Department.
2.tq: Use the department-name distinction to avoid a neighbouring-department trap.
2.sec: AP State Council of Science and Technology (APCOST) - state-level role

2.s: State science and technology councils such as APCOST receive support under which programme of the Department of Science and Technology?
2.x: APCOST and similar state councils receive support under the Department of Science and Technology’s State S&T Programme.
2.tq: Match the state institution with the correct DST support programme.
2.sec: AP State Council of Science and Technology (APCOST) - state-level role

2.s:
Consider the following statements regarding state science and technology councils:
1. They can provide research grants.
2. They can popularise science.
3. The Tamil Nadu State Council for Science and Technology works on translating academic research into use.
4. APCOST’s founding year and current programmes are specified as established features of its institutional role.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The stated institutional information does not specify APCOST’s founding year or current programmes, so statement 4 is not correct.
2.tq: Separate stated functions from details that are not established by the institutional description.
2.sec: AP State Council of Science and Technology (APCOST) - state-level role

2.s: Which one of the following schemes is intended for meritorious girl students studying in Classes 9 to 12 and is implemented with the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti?
2.x: Vigyan Jyoti targets meritorious girl students in Classes 9 to 12 and is implemented with the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti.
2.tq: Identify the scheme from its precise target group and implementing organisation.

2.s:
Consider the following statements regarding DST schemes for women and inclusion in STEM:
1. KIRAN is an umbrella programme for women scientists, including those returning after a career break.
2. WISE supports women's re-entry and career advancement in STEM.
3. GATI seeks gender equity through structural reforms in academic and research institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: All three statements are correct. KIRAN, WISE and GATI address women scientists, career advancement and institutional gender equity respectively.
2.tq: Check each scheme against its distinctive beneficiary or institutional purpose.
2.sec: DST schemes for women and inclusion in STEM → target group

2.s: The WiSLP scheme is primarily associated with which of the following groups?
o: Meritorious boys studying in Classes 9 to 12
Universities selected on the basis of publication output
Women scientists at the early and mid-career stages
2.x: WiSLP, or Women in Space and Allied Science Leadership Programme, is meant for early- and mid-career women scientists and is associated with the British Council.
2.tq: Discriminate between closely related women-focused schemes by their career stage.
2.sec: DST schemes for women and inclusion in STEM → target group

2.s: The SEED programme has established 52 STI Hubs primarily for which of the following groups?
o: Meritorious girl students in Classes 9 to 12
Women scientists returning after career breaks
2.x: SEED, or Science for Equity, Empowerment and Development, has established 52 STI Hubs for SC/ST communities.
2.tq: Link the numerical detail with the programme's specific inclusion target.
2.sec: DST schemes for women and inclusion in STEM → target group

2.s: SATHI is the acronym for:
o: Shared Analytical Technology for Higher Innovation
Science and Technology Assistance for Higher Institutions
2.x: SATHI stands for Sophisticated Analytical & Technical Help Institutes.
2.tq: Test the exact official expansion of a science-infrastructure acronym.
2.sec: DST research-infrastructure schemes → full form + purpose

2.s: Which one of the following best describes the purpose of SATHI?
o: Providing shared high-end analytical instruments to academia, start-ups and MSMEs
Providing research grants to universities according to publication output
Awarding school students for innovation and providing PhD fellowships
Upgrading only the buildings of women postgraduate colleges
2.x: SATHI provides shared access to high-end analytical instruments for academia, start-ups and MSMEs.
2.tq: Apply the scheme's purpose to the institutions that would use its facilities.
2.sec: DST research-infrastructure schemes → full form + purpose

2.s: FIST refers to which of the following?
o: Fund for Institutional Support to Technology
Fund for Improvement of S&T Infrastructure in universities and higher educational institutions
Facility for Innovation and Science Technology
2.x: FIST means Fund for Improvement of S&T Infrastructure in universities and higher educational institutions.
2.tq: Use the exact expansion rather than a look-alike interpretation of the acronym.
2.sec: DST research-infrastructure schemes → full form + purpose

2.s: The principal purpose of FIST is to:
o: Upgrade laboratories and equipment of academic departments
Support women scientists returning after a career break
Rank universities on their publication output
Establish STI Hubs for SC/ST communities
2.x: FIST is intended for upgrading laboratories and equipment in departments of universities and higher educational institutions.
2.tq: Separate infrastructure-upgrade schemes from fellowships, rankings and inclusion programmes.
2.sec: DST research-infrastructure schemes → full form + purpose

2.s: Which of the following correctly describes INSPIRE?
o: Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research; it draws young talent into science from school awards to PhD fellowships and faculty posts
Institute Network for Science and Professional Research Education; it provides shared instruments to MSMEs
Innovation Support Programme for Research Equipment; it upgrades departmental laboratories
Indian Network for Scientific Promotion and Research Excellence; it provides only university publication grants
2.x: INSPIRE stands for Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research and covers a continuum from school awards to PhD fellowships and faculty posts to attract young talent to science.
2.tq: Use the full-form-and-purpose combination to reject swapped institutional functions.
2.sec: DST research-infrastructure schemes → full form + purpose

2.s: PURSE is associated with which one of the following purposes?
o: Career advancement of women scientists in STEM
Research grants to universities ranked on publication output
Laboratory and equipment upgrades of departments
Shared high-end analytical instruments for start-ups and MSMEs
2.x: PURSE, or Promotion of University Research and Scientific Excellence, provides research grants to universities ranked on publication output.
2.tq: Match the scheme with its distinctive basis for support.
2.sec: DST research-infrastructure schemes → full form + purpose

2.s: National Technology Day is observed on 11 May to mark which of the following events?
o: The discovery of the Raman Effect in 1928
The establishment of the Department of Science and Technology
The launch of the INSPIRE programme
2.x: National Technology Day on 11 May commemorates the Pokhran-II nuclear tests conducted in 1998.
2.tq: Distinguish the technology observance from the separately commemorated science observance.
2.sec: National Science Day and National Technology Day

2.s:

1. India was ranked 38th in the Global Innovation Index 2025.
2. India ranked sixth in the world in patent filing activity according to WIPO 2023.
3. India occupied the 49th position out of 133 in the Network Readiness Index 2024.

2.x: All three statements are correct: India ranked 38th in GII 2025, sixth globally in WIPO 2023 patent filing activity, and 49th of 133 in the Network Readiness Index 2024.
2.tq: Check each ranking independently before selecting the coded combination.
2.sec: Innovation rankings - GII, patents

2.s: According to WIPO 2023 data, India's position in global patent filing activity was:
2.x: India ranked sixth in the world in patent filing activity according to WIPO 2023.
2.tq: Match the rank with the correct indicator rather than with a similarly reported index.

2.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India's performance in the Network Readiness Index?
2.x: India ranked 49th out of 133 in the Network Readiness Index 2024, up from 79th in 2019.
2.tq: Track both the latest rank and the direction of change across years.
2.sec: Innovation rankings - GII, patents

2.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Draft National Health Research Policy, 2026 is correct?
o: It was approved as the RDI Scheme on 1 July 2025.
It is the fifth national science and technology policy prepared by the Department of Science and Technology.
It focuses exclusively on patent filing activity and innovation rankings.
It is the first unified health-research framework and was prepared by the Department of Health Research.
2.x: The Draft National Health Research Policy, 2026, prepared by the Department of Health Research, is described as the first unified health-research framework.
2.tq: Identify the responsible department and distinguish a draft policy from a separate approved scheme.

2.s: The Draft National Health Research Policy, 2026 proposes raising public health-research spending from 0.024% of GDP to which levels by 2037 and 2047 respectively?
2.x: The draft policy proposes increasing public health-research spending from 0.024% of GDP to 0.072% by 2037 and 0.15% by 2047.

2.sec: Universal angles

2.s: Which governance arrangement is proposed under the Draft National Health Research Policy, 2026?
o: Single-tier governance under the Department of Science and Technology
2.x: The Draft National Health Research Policy, 2026 proposes a three-tier governance structure.
2.tq: Identify the policy architecture from the exact structural descriptor.
2.sec: Universal angles

2.s:
Arrange the following national science and technology policy milestones in chronological order:
A. STIP 2020
B. SPR 1958
C. Science and Technology Policy 1983
D. Science and Technology Policy 2003
2.x: The correct sequence is SPR 1958, Science and Technology Policy 1983, Science and Technology Policy 2003 and STIP 2020.
2.tq: Fix the first and last milestones, then place the intermediate policies by year.
2.sec: Universal angles

2.s: Which of the following statements about national science and technology policies is correct?
o: STIP 2020 preceded SPR 1958 and was the second national policy.

12.x: An oval represents start or end; a diamond represents decision, a parallelogram input/output and a rectangle a process.

12.s: Pseudocode is best described as
o: an English-like outline of a program or algorithm
12.x: Pseudocode expresses program logic in an English-like form without requiring the exact syntax of a programming language.
12.tq: Distinguish a planning representation from executable code and hardware.
12.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems  [GK]

12.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its number-system base?
12.x: Binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal have bases 2, 8, 10 and 16 respectively.
12.tq: Check the base rather than the familiar name of the number system.
12.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

12.s: The hexadecimal number (FF)₁₆ is equal to
12.x: F represents 15, so FF equals 15 × 16 + 15 = 255.
12.tq: Convert hexadecimal by applying place value and digit value.
12.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

12.s: The binary number (1010)₂ is equal to
12.x: (1010)₂ equals 8 + 0 + 2 + 0, which is 10 in decimal notation.
12.tq: Evaluate binary digits using powers of two.
12.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

12.s: Which one of the following gates is a universal gate?
12.x: NAND and NOR are universal gates because basic logic functions can be implemented using either of them.
12.tq: Recall the special classification of universal logic gates.
12.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

12.s: An XOR gate produces output 1 when
12.x: For the stated two-input condition, XOR gives 1 when the inputs differ.
12.tq: Apply the truth condition rather than confusing XOR with OR.
12.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

12.s:
Consider the following Boolean identities:
1. A + A = A
2. A · A′ = 0
3. (A + B)′ = A′ · B′
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: All three are valid Boolean identities; the third is De Morgan's law.
12.tq: Verify each algebraic identity independently before selecting the combined code.
12.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

12.s: The laws represented by (A + B)′ = A′ · B′ are associated with
12.x: The stated complement relation is De Morgan's law within Boolean algebra, developed in the Boolean tradition associated here with George Boole.
12.tq: Identify the named logical law from its algebraic expression.
12.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

12.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its file type?
12.x: MP4 stands for MPEG-4 Part 14 and is a video file format. MP3 is audio, PDF is a document format and MOV is a video format.
12.tq: Start from the sure file-type pair and eliminate the swapped categories.
12.sec: File formats and acronyms → expansion or type  [APPSC]

12.s: The acronym MP3 stands for
12.x: MP3 expands to MPEG-1 Audio Layer 3 and is an audio format.
12.tq: Test the exact expansion rather than identifying the general file category.
12.sec: File formats and acronyms → expansion or type  [APPSC]

12.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
12.x: PNG stands for Portable Network Graphics, not Portable Network Graphics Interface. AVI, MOV and GIF are correctly matched.
12.tq: Find the altered word in an otherwise familiar acronym expansion.
12.sec: File formats and acronyms → expansion or type  [APPSC]

12.s:
Consider the following statements regarding ASCII:
1. ASCII is a 7-bit character-encoding scheme.
2. ASCII represents 128 characters.
3. Unicode extends the character-representation capability of ASCII.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: ASCII is a 7-bit code representing 128 characters, while Unicode extends the range of character representation. All three statements are correct.
12.tq: Check each numerical and relationship statement before selecting the combined code.
12.sec: File formats and acronyms → expansion or type  [APPSC]

12.s: JPEG is primarily associated with which of the following?
12.x: JPEG, or Joint Photographic Experts Group, is an image format commonly associated with lossy compression.
12.tq: Distinguish the file format’s information type from unrelated compression categories.
12.sec: File formats and acronyms → expansion or type  [APPSC]

12.s: Which generation of computers used vacuum tubes as its core technology?
12.x: First-generation computers, broadly dating from the 1940s to 1956, used vacuum tubes. ENIAC and UNIVAC are associated with this generation.
12.tq: Link the generation number with its defining core technology.
12.sec: Computing history - generations, inventors  [APPSC]

12.s:
Arrange the following computer generations in chronological order of their core technologies:
A. Integrated circuits
B. Vacuum tubes
C. Microprocessors
D. Transistors
12.x: The correct sequence is vacuum tubes, transistors, integrated circuits and microprocessors, corresponding broadly to the first through fourth generations.
12.tq: Fix the first and last technologies, then place the intermediate generations.
12.sec: Computing history - generations, inventors  [APPSC]

12.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the fifth generation of computers?
o: Artificial intelligence, ULSI and parallel processing
12.x: The fifth generation is associated with artificial intelligence, ultra-large-scale integration and parallel processing.
12.tq: Use the distinctive technology cluster to identify the generation.
12.sec: Computing history - generations, inventors  [APPSC]

12.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Charles Babbage — Analytical Engine
b. Ada Lovelace — First programmer
c. Douglas Engelbart — Computer mouse
d. Larry Tesler — Cut, copy and paste
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
12.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Babbage is associated with the Analytical Engine, Lovelace with the first program, Engelbart with the mouse, and Tesler with cut, copy and paste.
12.tq: Match each inventor with the specific contribution, avoiding famous-name substitution.
12.sec: Computing history - generations, inventors  [APPSC]

12.s: Who is associated with the creation of the World Wide Web in 1989?
12.x: Tim Berners-Lee is associated with the World Wide Web, developed in 1989.
12.tq: Identify the person linked to the named invention and its date.
12.sec: Computing history - generations, inventors  [APPSC]

12.s: The stored-program architecture is associated with
12.x: John von Neumann is associated with the stored-program architecture.
12.tq: Discriminate between closely related pioneers by their specific contribution.
12.sec: Computing history - generations, inventors  [APPSC]

12.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding early Indian computing achievements?
1. TIFRAC was the first indigenous computer of India.
2. PARAM 8000 was the first Indian supercomputer.
3. PARAM 8000 was developed in 1991 by C-DAC under Vijay Bhatkar.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
12.x: TIFRAC was India’s first indigenous computer. PARAM 8000, developed in 1991 by C-DAC under Vijay Bhatkar, was the first Indian supercomputer.
12.tq: Combine the institution, year and achievement only after checking each statement.
12.sec: Computing history - generations, inventors  [APPSC]

12.s: In the context of computing history, “technology preservation” refers to a
o: method of storing data in RAM
12.x: “Technology preservation” is associated with a computer museum, where earlier technologies are retained and displayed.
12.tq: Recognise the exact term-to-meaning association instead of interpreting it literally.
12.sec: Computing history - generations, inventors  [APPSC]

12.s: Word length of a computer refers to the
o: number of bits handled by the CPU at one time
physical length of a memory module
number of characters stored in a file name
number of instructions executed in one minute
12.x: Word length is the number of bits that the CPU can handle at once, such as 32-bit or 64-bit processing.
12.tq: Separate a processing-width term from storage and speed terms.
12.sec: Computer performance terms - word length, bandwidth, clock speed, MIPS, FLOPS  [APPSC]

12.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Clock speed — floating-point operations per second
12.x: Bandwidth measures data-transfer rate in bits per second. Clock speed is measured in hertz, MIPS denotes million instructions per second, and word length is measured in bits.
12.tq: Match each performance term with its precise unit or meaning.
12.sec: Computer performance terms - word length, bandwidth, clock speed, MIPS, FLOPS  [APPSC]

12.s: MIPS is the abbreviation for
12.x: MIPS means million instructions per second and is used to express instruction-processing performance.
12.tq: Test the exact expansion of a performance acronym.
12.sec: Computer performance terms - word length, bandwidth, clock speed, MIPS, FLOPS  [APPSC]

12.s: The clock speed of a computer is generally measured in
12.x: Clock speed is measured in hertz, commonly expressed as gigahertz (GHz).
12.tq: Distinguish frequency units from data-transfer and storage units.
12.sec: Computer performance terms - word length, bandwidth, clock speed, MIPS, FLOPS  [APPSC]

12.s: FLOPS is used to express
12.x: FLOPS means floating-point operations per second and is used particularly to indicate supercomputer performance.
12.tq: Expand the acronym and connect it with the correct performance measure.
12.sec: Computer performance terms - word length, bandwidth, clock speed, MIPS, FLOPS  [APPSC]

12.s: Which benchmark measures floating-point performance while solving large dense linear systems and forms the basis of world supercomputer rankings?
12.x: The Linpack, or HPL, benchmark measures floating-point power in solving large dense linear systems and is used for world supercomputer rankings.
12.tq: Identify the benchmark from its distinctive workload and ranking application.
12.sec: Computer performance terms - word length, bandwidth, clock speed, MIPS, FLOPS  [APPSC]

12.s: A speedometer and a thermometer illustrate the use of which type of computer or computing principle?
12.x: Analog computers or systems represent continuous quantities; speedometers and thermometers are examples.
12.tq: Infer the computer type from whether the quantity is continuous or discrete.
12.sec: Computer types - analog, digital, hybrid, PC, supercomputer, quantum  [APPSC]

12.s: Which one of the following is characteristic of a digital computer?
o: It processes only continuously varying physical quantities.
It necessarily combines an ECG monitor with a thermometer.
It processes discrete data, commonly in binary form.
It uses qubits as its basic information unit.
12.x: Digital computers process discrete data, commonly represented in binary form. PCs are common examples.
12.tq: Separate discrete binary processing from analog and quantum characteristics.
12.sec: Computer types - analog, digital, hybrid, PC, supercomputer, quantum  [APPSC]

12.s: A hospital intensive-care monitor that combines continuous measurements with digital processing is best classified as a
12.x: Hybrid computers combine analog and digital features. Hospital ICU monitors and ECG systems are examples.
12.tq: Apply the both-features clue to identify a hybrid system.
12.sec: Computer types - analog, digital, hybrid, PC, supercomputer, quantum  [APPSC]

12.s:
Which of the following are included among personal or microcomputer devices?
1. Desktop
2. Laptop
3. Tablet
4. Smartwatch
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
12.x: Desktops, laptops, tablets and smartwatches are all included among personal or microcomputer devices. Smartphones, fitness trackers and AR glasses also fall within this broad group.
12.tq: Recognise the inclusive device category rather than restricting personal computers to desktops.
12.sec: Computer types - analog, digital, hybrid, PC, supercomputer, quantum  [APPSC]

12.s: Mini and mainframe computers are primarily characterised as
12.x: Mini and mainframe computers are multi-user machines used in organisations.
12.tq: Match the computer class with its scale and user pattern.
12.sec: Computer types - analog, digital, hybrid, PC, supercomputer, quantum  [APPSC]

12.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a supercomputer?
o: A computer with the highest processing power, commonly expressed in FLOPS
A computer with the lowest processing speed, measured only in bytes
A computer that represents information only through qubits
A computer used exclusively as a word processor
12.x: Supercomputers provide the highest processing power and their speed is commonly expressed in FLOPS.
12.tq: Use the defining performance feature to distinguish supercomputers from other types.
12.sec: Computer types - analog, digital, hybrid, PC, supercomputer, quantum  [APPSC]

12.s: According to the ISC 2026 ranking referred to here, the world’s fastest supercomputer is
o: El Capitan of the United States
12.x: China’s LineShine topped the ISC 2026 supercomputer list, replacing the United States’ El Capitan.
12.tq: Track the current ranking and the country-replacement relationship carefully.
12.sec: Computer types - analog, digital, hybrid, PC, supercomputer, quantum  [APPSC]

12.s:
Consider the following statements about Param Shakti at IIT Madras:
1. It was launched by MeitY.
2. It has a capacity of 3.1 petaflops.
3. It uses C-DAC RUDRA servers.
4. It operates with open-source AlmaLinux.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: Param Shakti at IIT Madras was launched by MeitY, has 3.1 petaflops capacity, uses C-DAC RUDRA servers and runs open-source AlmaLinux.
12.tq: Verify all institutional, numerical and technical attributes before choosing the complete code.
12.sec: Computer types - analog, digital, hybrid, PC, supercomputer, quantum  [APPSC]

12.s: Param Shakti at IIT Madras was funded under the
12.x: Param Shakti was funded under the National Supercomputing Mission.
12.tq: Identify the correct government mission associated with the named installation.
12.sec: Computer types - analog, digital, hybrid, PC, supercomputer, quantum  [APPSC]

12.s:
Which of the following are associated with quantum computing?
1. Superposition
2. Entanglement
3. Cryptography
4. Optimisation
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
12.x: Quantum computing uses superposition and entanglement and has applications in cryptography and optimisation. All four statements are correct.
12.tq: Combine the underlying principles with the listed application areas.
12.sec: Computer types - analog, digital, hybrid, PC, supercomputer, quantum  [APPSC]

12.s: Q-Day refers to the point at which quantum computers may be capable of
o: breaking RSA-2048 public-key encryption using Shor’s algorithm
converting every file into PDF format
increasing the clock speed of classical processors
12.x: Q-Day denotes the anticipated point when quantum computers can break RSA-2048 public-key encryption through Shor’s algorithm, proposed in 1994.
12.tq: Link the specialised term to its specific security consequence and algorithm.
12.sec: Computer types - analog, digital, hybrid, PC, supercomputer, quantum  [APPSC]

12.s: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) is best understood as an umbrella term covering devices and applications used to
o: replace all forms of human communication
access, store, transmit and manipulate digital information
12.x: ICT covers devices and applications used to access, store, transmit and manipulate digital information, including mobiles, networks, software, the internet and satellites.
12.tq: Choose the comprehensive definition rather than an exclusive or extreme description.
12.sec: Universal angles

12.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or debate associated with ICT?
12.x: Privacy risks, the digital divide, job insecurity and over-reliance on technology are identified concerns. Guaranteed elimination of technological dependence is not such a criticism.
12.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated group of ICT concerns.
12.sec: Universal angles

12.s:
ICT aims to facilitate communication among which of the following?
1. Human and human
2. Human and machine
3. Machine and machine
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
12.x: ICT aims at efficient human-human, human-machine and machine-to-machine communication. Therefore, all three forms are included.
12.tq: Read the communication relationships separately before selecting the combined option.
12.sec: Universal angles

13.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the function of HTML tags in a webpage?
o: They define and mark up the structure of text and other content
They assign numerical IP addresses to webpages
13.x: HTML tags mark up and structure the text and other content of webpages. Encryption and indexing are performed by other technologies or services.
13.tq: Distinguish the structural role of HTML from the functions of encryption, addressing and search.
13.sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

13.s:
Consider the following statements regarding web technologies:
1. A web server stores webpages and sends them when requested.
2. A web browser requests webpages and displays them on the screen.
3. A search engine indexes webpages so that they can be found.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: All three statements are correct. The server stores and serves pages, the browser displays them, and the search engine indexes them for discovery.
13.tq: Separate the closely related functions of the server, browser and search engine.
13.sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

13.s: HTTP primarily specifies which of the following?
o: How messages pass between web browsers and web servers
How domain names are converted into IP addresses
How wireless devices communicate within a PAN
How e-mails are downloaded to a device
13.x: HTTP specifies the communication of messages between web browsers and web servers. DNS, POP3 and Bluetooth serve different functions.
13.tq: Match the protocol with its immediate communication function rather than with a neighbouring networking function.
13.sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

13.s: Which one of the following represents the correct order of the principal parts of a URL?
o: Protocol, domain name, path to the file
Protocol, path to the file, domain name
13.x: A URL contains the protocol, such as https://, followed by the domain name and the path to the file.
13.tq: Test the internal order of URL components instead of merely recalling its expansion.
13.sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

13.s: The principal role of the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) is to:
o: Assign MAC addresses to network cards
Operate the global DNS root servers
13.x: W3C develops and maintains web standards so that webpages function consistently across different browsers.
13.tq: Identify the responsible body by its standard-setting function.
13.sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

13.s:
Which of the following constitutes the core front-end technologies mentioned in relation to modern web development?
1. HTML5
2. CSS3
3. JavaScript
4. DHCP
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript are core front-end technologies. DHCP is a network protocol that assigns IP addresses automatically.
13.tq: Find the unrelated networking protocol among front-end web technologies.
13.sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

13.s:
With reference to Web 3.0, consider the following statements:
1. It represents the third generation of the web.
2. It changes how the web is used, how sites are managed and how services are delivered.
3. OCEN is linked with Web 3.0 and aims to democratise lending.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: Web 3.0 is the third generation of the web and involves changes in usage, site management and service delivery. OCEN seeks to democratise lending and improve credit terms for small borrowers.
13.tq: Combine the definition, scope and associated initiative without confusing Web 3.0 with a single application.
13.sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

13.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its description?
o: Surface web — not indexed by search engines
Deep web — entirely associated with illegal markets
Dark web — hidden subset of the deep web requiring tools such as Tor or I2P
Surface web — accessible only through anonymous networks
13.x: The dark web is a small hidden subset of the deep web and is associated with anonymous access through tools such as Tor or I2P. The surface web is indexed, while the deep web is not necessarily malicious.
13.tq: Use the defining access and indexing features to separate surface, deep and dark web.
13.sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

13.s:
Arrange the following layers of the web in descending order of their approximate share:
A. Dark web
B. Surface web
C. Deep web
Select the correct sequence.
13.x: The deep web accounts for approximately 90–95%, the surface web about 4–5%, and the dark web is a small hidden subset.
13.tq: Order categories by relative size, beginning with the largest share.
13.sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

13.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
13.x: Indexed public webpages belong to the surface web, not the dark web. E-mail inboxes, net banking and intranets are examples of deep-web content.
13.tq: Identify the one reversed classification by applying the indexing criterion.
13.sec: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0  [APPSC]

13.s: ARPANET, established in 1969, was developed under which organisation and is regarded as the forerunner of the Internet?
13.x: ARPANET was developed under the United States Department of Defense in 1969 and became the forerunner of the Internet.
13.tq: Link the historical network with its sponsoring organisation and legacy.
13.sec: Internet history - ARPANET, WWW inventor, first Indian ISPs  [APPSC]

13.s: The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) was founded in which year?
13.x: Tim Berners-Lee founded the W3C in 1994. The other years correspond to ERNET, the invention of the WWW and the emergence of Satyam Infoway as a private ISP.
13.tq: Discriminate between closely related milestones by their years.
13.sec: Internet history - ARPANET, WWW inventor, first Indian ISPs  [APPSC]

13.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the Indian Internet milestones in chronological order?
o: Public internet by VSNL, ERNET, Satyam Infoway
Satyam Infoway, ERNET, public internet by VSNL
ERNET, public internet by VSNL, Satyam Infoway
ERNET, Satyam Infoway, public internet by VSNL
13.x: ERNET began in 1986, public internet was launched by VSNL on 15 August 1995, and Satyam Infoway became the first private ISP in 1998.
13.tq: Use the first, middle and last dates to establish the sequence.
13.sec: Internet history - ARPANET, WWW inventor, first Indian ISPs  [APPSC]

13.s: On which date was public Internet service launched in India by VSNL?
13.x: VSNL launched public Internet service in India on 15 August 1995. ERNET had been established earlier as an academic network in 1986.
13.tq: Distinguish the public-service launch date from the academic-network and private-ISP dates.
13.sec: Internet history - ARPANET, WWW inventor, first Indian ISPs  [APPSC]

13.s: Which of the following was India’s academic network established in 1986?
13.x: ERNET was India’s academic network established in 1986. VSNL launched public internet service in 1995, while Satyam Infoway became the first private ISP in 1998.
13.tq: Match the network name with its historical category and year.
13.sec: Internet history - ARPANET, WWW inventor, first Indian ISPs  [APPSC]

13.s: Which notation is characteristic of an IPv4 address?
o: Six hexadecimal pairs separated by hyphens
Four decimal octets separated by dots
A domain name followed by a file path
Eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons
13.x: IPv4 uses dotted-decimal notation, such as 192.168.1.1. IPv6 uses eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons, whereas six hexadecimal pairs describe a MAC address.
13.tq: Separate the notations of IPv4, IPv6 and MAC addressing.
13.sec: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes  [APPSC]

13.s: Which one of the following correctly describes an IPv6 address?
o: A 64-bit address used only for multicast
A 48-bit address burnt into a network card
A 32-bit address written only in dotted decimal
A 128-bit address written as eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons
13.x: IPv6 is 128 bits long and is written as eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons. A 48-bit physical address refers to MAC addressing.
13.tq: Use length and notation together to distinguish IPv6 from IPv4 and MAC addresses.
13.sec: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes  [APPSC]

13.s: A MAC address is best described as a:
o: 48-bit physical address burnt into the network card and used at the data link layer
16-bit address used only by web browsers
32-bit logical address used at the network layer
13.x: A MAC address is a 48-bit physical address, equal to 6 bytes or 12 hexadecimal digits, generally burnt into the network card and used at the data link layer.
13.tq: Combine the address length, physical nature and OSI-layer association.
13.sec: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes  [APPSC]

13.s:
Which of the following pairs correctly represents IPv4 address classes by their first-octet ranges?
1. Class A — 1 to 126
2. Class B — 128 to 191
3. Class C — 192 to 223
4. Class D — 240 to 255
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: Classes A, B and C have ranges 1–126, 128–191 and 192–223 respectively. Class D is 224–239 for multicast; 240–255 is Class E for experimental use.
13.tq: Check each numerical range against the class boundary, especially the swapped D and E ranges.
13.sec: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes  [APPSC]

13.s: The address range 224–239 in IPv4 is associated with:
13.x: The first-octet range 224–239 constitutes Class D, used for multicast. Class E occupies 240–255, while 127.x.x.x is reserved for loopback.
13.tq: Test the boundary ranges of the IPv4 classes directly.
13.sec: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes  [APPSC]

13.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
13.x: The 127.x.x.x range is used for loopback. Class D multicast is 224–239, Class E experimental is 240–255, and 192–223 is Class C.
13.tq: Find the correctly matched exception among deliberately interchanged class ranges.
13.sec: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes  [APPSC]

13.s: DNS performs which of the following functions?
o: Assigns MAC addresses to network cards
Converts human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses
13.x: DNS acts as the Internet’s directory by translating human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses.
13.tq: Identify the service needed when a user knows a name but the network requires an IP address.
13.sec: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes  [APPSC]

13.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the wireless standard?
13.x: Bluetooth uses IEEE 802.15.1 and is a personal area network technology. Wi-Fi uses IEEE 802.11 and is associated with wireless LANs.
13.tq: Start from the standard number to distinguish Bluetooth from Wi-Fi.
13.sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

13.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Bluetooth and Wi-Fi:
1. Bluetooth generally has a short range of about 10 metres for a class 2 device.
2. Wi-Fi generally provides coverage over a longer range, such as a whole building.
3. Bluetooth operates only in the 5 GHz band.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: Bluetooth class 2 devices have a short range of approximately 10 metres, while Wi-Fi generally covers a larger area. Bluetooth operates in the 2.4 GHz ISM band, not only in 5 GHz.
13.tq: Use range and frequency comparisons to reject the absolute frequency claim.
13.sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

13.s: Which one of the following statements about Wi-Fi frequency bands is correct?
o: Wi-Fi operates only in the 6 GHz band.
Wi-Fi uses the 2.4 GHz band only for Bluetooth compatibility.
Wi-Fi operates in 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands, with 6 GHz available in Wi-Fi 6E.
Wi-Fi operates only in the 2.4 GHz band.
13.x: Wi-Fi uses the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands; Wi-Fi 6E also includes the 6 GHz band. Bluetooth uses the 2.4 GHz ISM band.
13.tq: Test the frequency-band comparison and the Wi-Fi 6E exception.
13.sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

13.s:
Which of the following devices commonly operates in the 2.4 GHz range?
1. Microwave oven
2. Cordless phone
3. Bluetooth device
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: Microwave ovens, cordless phones and Bluetooth devices are among the devices associated with the 2.4 GHz range.
13.tq: Use the shared-band idea to identify all applicable devices.
13.sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

13.s: The 2019 APPSC key identified which version as the latest version of Bluetooth?
13.x: The 2019 APPSC key treated Bluetooth 5.1 as the latest version. This is a time-specific reference and should not be confused with later versions.
13.tq: Recognise the dated examination reference rather than applying an unspecified current-version claim.
13.sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

13.s: Which one of the following technologies links devices directly without requiring a LAN?
13.x: Wi-Fi Direct enables devices to connect directly without a LAN. DNS resolves names, DHCP assigns IP addresses and Li-Fi transmits data through LED light.
13.tq: Select the technology that satisfies the stated direct-connect requirement.
13.sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

13.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes Li-Fi from Wi-Fi?
o: Li-Fi carries data on LED light and can provide better bandwidth and security than Wi-Fi.
Li-Fi operates only through telephone lines and has no wireless application.
Li-Fi is a form of DNS-based addressing.
Li-Fi is restricted to Bluetooth personal area networks.
13.x: Li-Fi transmits data using LED light and is described as offering better bandwidth and security than Wi-Fi.
13.tq: Use the transmission medium to distinguish Li-Fi from radio-based Wi-Fi.
13.sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

13.s: NFC is characterised by which of the following features?
o: Operation over several kilometres at gigabit speed
Operation only at a few centimetres with a rate of 106–424 kbps
Operation throughout a building using 5 GHz only
13.x: NFC works only over a few centimetres and has a stated data rate of 106–424 kbps.
13.tq: Combine the very short range with the specified data-rate interval.
13.sec: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices  [APPSC]

13.s: Which protocol is primarily used for reliable delivery of data in the TCP/IP suite?
13.x: Within TCP/IP, TCP ensures reliable delivery, while IP addresses and routes packets.
13.tq: Separate the transport reliability function of TCP from the addressing and routing function of IP.
13.sec: Protocols → function; protocol elements  [APPSC]

13.s: Which one of the following protocols transfers webpages, with its secure version encrypting browser-server traffic through TLS?
13.x: HTTP transfers webpages, while HTTPS encrypts browser-server traffic using TLS.
13.tq: Match the protocol pair with web transfer and security rather than with mail or file transfer.
13.sec: Protocols → function; protocol elements  [APPSC]

13.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: POP3 — downloading mail to one device, usually deleting it from the server
IMAP — permanently deleting mail from the server after downloading it to one device
13.x: IMAP keeps mail on the server and synchronises it across devices. POP3 generally downloads mail to one device and usually deletes it from the server.
13.tq: Distinguish the confusable mail protocols by their treatment of messages on the server.
13.sec: Protocols → function; protocol elements  [APPSC]

13.s: A user wants the same e-mail account to remain synchronised across several devices. Which protocol is most suitable?
13.x: IMAP keeps mail on the server and synchronises it across devices. POP3 is generally intended for downloading mail to one device.
13.tq: Infer the protocol from the practical requirement of multi-device synchronisation.
13.sec: Protocols → function; protocol elements  [APPSC]

13.s: Which protocol automatically assigns IP addresses to devices on a network?
13.x: DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically. DNS translates names into IP addresses, while HTTP and TCP perform different communication functions.
13.tq: Identify the protocol by its automatic address-assignment function.
13.sec: Protocols → function; protocol elements  [APPSC]

13.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Protocol element)
A. Syntax
B. Semantics
C. Timing

List-II (Meaning)
1. Meaning of each field
2. Format of data
3. When and how fast to send

option_a
13.x: Syntax specifies the format of data, semantics specifies the meaning of each field, and timing specifies when and how fast data is sent.
13.tq: Start from the sure pair ‘syntax–format’ and complete the protocol-element mapping.
13.sec: Protocols → function; protocol elements  [APPSC]

13.s:
Assertion (A): HTTPS provides greater security for browser-server communication than HTTP.
Reason (R): HTTPS encrypts the traffic between the browser and the server through TLS.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
13.x: Both statements are true, and TLS-based encryption directly explains why HTTPS provides greater security than HTTP.
13.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the security difference between HTTP and HTTPS.
13.sec: Protocols → function; protocol elements  [APPSC]

13.s: A network confined to the personal devices of an individual, generally using Bluetooth, is known as:
13.x: PAN stands for Personal Area Network and connects an individual's nearby devices, commonly through Bluetooth.
13.tq: Use the coverage-area clue to distinguish network types.
13.sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

13.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the usual geographical coverage of a MAN?
13.x: A Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) generally covers a city, placing it between a LAN and a WAN in geographical extent.
13.tq: Split the options by geographical scale.
13.sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

13.s: A network that spans a large geographical area and links LANs at different locations is called:
13.x: A Wide Area Network (WAN) connects networks over large areas; the Internet is an example of a global WAN.
13.tq: Match the definition with the widest network category.
13.sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

13.s: A Virtual Private Network primarily provides:
o: A replacement for all network protocols
A wireless connection restricted to one room
A physical cable exclusively owned by a user
An encrypted tunnel over a public network
13.x: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel through a public network, improving the privacy of communication.
13.tq: Identify the function rather than the physical form of the network.
13.sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

13.s:
Consider the following statements regarding network topologies:
1. In a bus topology, all nodes share one backbone cable.
2. In a star topology, failure of one node normally isolates the entire network.
3. In a ring topology, each node is linked to two neighbouring nodes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. In a star topology, failure of one node is generally isolated; failure of the central hub can stop the network.
13.tq: Find the incorrect resilience statement before selecting the code.
13.sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

13.s: Which topology is characterised by every node being connected to every other node?
13.x: In a mesh topology, every node is linked to every other node, making it highly resilient but costly.
13.tq: Use the complete-connectivity clue.
13.sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

13.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Tree topology — It has no hierarchical structure
Bus topology — Failure of one node isolates only that node
Star topology — Failure of the central hub can stop all nodes
Ring topology — Every node is connected to every other node
13.x: In a star topology, all nodes depend on the central hub or switch; its failure can stop the entire network.
13.tq: Test the resilience consequence associated with each layout.
13.sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

13.s: A tree topology is best described as:
o: A single circular connection of nodes
A topology in which every node has a direct link to every other node
A network using only one backbone cable
13.x: A tree topology combines star networks in a hierarchy. Failure of a parent can affect the branch below it.
13.tq: Match the structural description with the topology name.
13.sec: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN  [APPSC]

13.s: ICANN, established in 1998 as a United States non-profit organisation, is primarily associated with:
o: Coordinating the global domain name system and IP address allocation
13.x: ICANN coordinates the global Domain Name System and IP address allocation. It was established in 1998 as a US non-profit organisation.
13.tq: Use the organisation-function and year combination.
13.sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

13.s:
Consider the following statements about NIXI:
1. It was established in 2003.
2. It is a not-for-profit organisation under MeitY.
3. It runs the .in registry and IRINN.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: NIXI was established in 2003, functions as a not-for-profit organisation under MeitY, and runs Internet exchange points, the .in registry and IRINN.
13.tq: Check each institutional detail before choosing the combined code.
13.sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

13.s: Which of the following is NOT a function associated with NIXI?
o: Coordinating the entire global DNS and global IP allocation system
13.x: NIXI performs Indian Internet exchange, .in registry and IRINN functions. Global DNS coordination and global IP allocation are associated with ICANN.
13.tq: Separate the national Internet institution from the global coordinating body.
13.sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

13.s: An Internationalised Domain Name (IDN) is a domain name that:
o: Works only without an Internet connection
Can be written only in hexadecimal characters
13.x: IDNs permit domain names in local scripts, such as .Bharat written in Devanagari.
13.tq: Use the meaning of 'internationalised' in the domain-name context.
13.sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

13.s: Universal Acceptance in the context of Internet governance means that:
o: All Internet content must be available without authentication
Every application and e-mail system should accept all valid domain names and e-mail IDs, including those in local scripts
Every country must use one common domain name
Only English-language domain names can be accessed universally
13.x: Universal Acceptance ensures that applications and e-mail systems correctly accept all valid domain names and e-mail IDs, including IDNs.
13.tq: Identify the inclusive technical standard rather than a content policy.
13.sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

13.s: BhashaNet, associated with MeitY and NIXI and launched in 2022, promotes:
o: Exclusive use of English on the Internet
13.x: BhashaNet promotes Universal Acceptance and the use of Indian-language Internet domain names and e-mail IDs; it is associated with MeitY-NIXI and the year 2022.
13.tq: Combine the initiative, institutional partners and objective.
13.sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

13.s:
Which provisions are associated with governmental blocking of online content in India?
1. Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000
2. Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000
3. Section 3 of the Telegraph Act, 1885
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: Sections 69A and 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 are associated with orders to ISPs and intermediaries for blocking content. Section 3 of the Telegraph Act is not the stated blocking provision.
13.tq: Eliminate the unrelated statutory provision.
13.sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

13.s: Which legislation replaced the Telegraph Act, 1885 and contains the power to suspend Internet services?
13.x: The Telecommunications Act, 2023 replaced the Telegraph Act and contains the power to suspend Internet services.
13.tq: Distinguish content-blocking provisions from the later telecommunications legislation.
13.sec: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)  [APPSC]

13.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Device)
a. Hub
b. Switch
c. Router
d. Modem

List-II (Primary role)
i. Routes packets using IP
 ii. Converts digital and analogue signals
 iii. Broadcasts data to all ports
 iv. Forwards frames using MAC addresses

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: A hub broadcasts to all ports, a switch forwards frames by MAC address, a router routes using IP, and a modem converts between digital and analogue signals.
13.tq: Start from the sure device-function pairs and complete the code.

13.s: A repeater is used primarily to:

13.tq: Match the device with its signal-level function.
